judged_text: The guest validation schema is hand-duplicated between this dialog (z.array + uniqueness refine) and addGuests.schema.ts on the server, and the two copies already diverge behaviorally: the client only rejects in-array duplicates while the server silently de-duplicates against existing attendees and blacklist entries. A user who submits a mix of one new and one already-attending email sees 'Guests added' with no indication that one email was silently skipped, and any future rule (max guests, blacklist awareness) must be implemented twice or the layers drift further.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows duplicated/ diverging validation: the client dialog defines its own `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` as `z.array(z.string().email()).refine(...)` in `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, enforcing only in-array uniqueness, while the server `addGuests.schema.ts` only validates `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` (no uniqueness) and `addGuests.handler.ts` applies additional filtering against existing attendees and `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` via `uniqueGuests = guests.filter(...)`. When a user submits a mix of new + already-attending/blacklisted emails, the server silently drops the non-addable ones and still returns success unless `uniqueGuests.length === 0`, and the UI always toasts `t("guests_added")` on success. This is a concrete consistency/UX and maintenance issue introduced by the change, though not a clear correctness defect per se.
